title_en: Supreme People's Court Publishes Typical Criminal Cases of Crimes Committed through the Internet
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court Publishes Typical Criminal Cases of Crimes Committed via the Internet

1. Defendant Feng Wendong — Intentional Homicide and Theft

(1) Basic Facts

Defendant Feng Wendong became acquainted with victim Zhang (female, died at age 24) through the Internet. On July 21, 2010, Feng Wendong went to a room in a residential complex in Fangchengyuan, Fengtai District, Beijing, which was jointly rented by Zhang and victim Li Zhongpeng (died at age 25), to engage in SM games (i.e., sexual sadomasochism games) with Zhang as agreed. At approximately 0:00 the next day, Feng Wendong got into an argument with Zhang and Li Zhongpeng over trivial matters. He then took a kitchen knife from Zhang's room and his own concealed dagger, and repeatedly stabbed and slashed their necks, chests, backs, and abdomens, causing both victims to die from acute hemorrhagic shock. Thereafter, Feng Wendong stole Li Zhongpeng's IBM laptop computer (valued at RMB 200), an OBEE brand mobile phone (valued at RMB 30), a wallet (valued at RMB 10), and over RMB 1,000 in cash, and fled the scene.

(2) Judgment

The Beijing Second Intermediate People's Court, after trial, found that the defendant Feng Wendong's act of killing two persons with a weapon after a dispute constituted the crime of intentional homicide; his act of stealing a relatively large amount of property from the victims after committing the homicide also constituted the crime of theft, and he should be punished for both crimes in accordance with the law. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Criminal Law, the Beijing Second Intermediate People's Court found the defendant Feng Wendong guilty of intentional homicide, sentencing him to death and deprivation of political rights for life; guilty of theft, sentencing him to fixed-term imprisonment of six months and a fine of RMB 500, and decided to execute the death penalty, deprivation of political rights for life, and a fine of RMB 500. After the judgment was pronounced, the defendant Feng Wendong appealed. The Beijing High People's Court, after trial in accordance with the law, ruled to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment, and reported the case to the Supreme People's Court for approval in accordance with the law. The Supreme People's Court, after review in accordance with the law, ruled to approve the death sentence for the defendant Feng Wendong.

(3) Typical Significance

Victim Zhang was originally male but underwent sex reassignment surgery in Thailand. For profit, Zhang operated a sexual sadomasochism training class and recruited partners for such games on the Internet. After learning through the Internet that Zhang was recruiting partners, defendant Feng Wendong contacted Zhang and voluntarily paid RMB 1,500 to have Zhang subject him to sexual sadomasochism. During the game, fearing that he would be tied up and killed by Zhang, they argued, and Feng Wendong stabbed Zhang and Li Zhongpeng, who shared the rental with Zhang, to death with a knife. The trial of this case clearly conveys to society the risks of the virtual nature of the Internet intruding into private life, and urges netizens to be vigilant, cultivate healthy and positive interests, and avoid bringing harm upon themselves.

2. Defendant Huang Su'an — Fraud

(1) Basic Facts

In October 2011, defendant Huang Su'an used a fabricated identity as a Chinese American to register on a dating website under the screen name "Xiangyi Yimo" and became acquainted with the female victim Xie. During their interactions, Huang Su'an falsely told Xie that the organization he worked for was about to launch a Panama Canal shipping route investment project, which would yield a return of six times the principal, with an investment threshold of RMB 7.05 million, and that before New Year's Day 2012, in addition to returning the principal, a return of RMB 18 million would be given. He used this to persuade Xie to invest. Xie believed this and agreed to invest in the project. On October 18, Xie transferred RMB 50,000 to an account designated by Huang Su'an. On October 20, Xie borrowed RMB 2 million at high interest from others and handed it over to Huang Su'an through bank transfers and other means. Thereafter, Xie borrowed another RMB 4.9 million at high interest and added RMB 100,000 of her own savings, handing the total to persons sent by Huang Su'an. When Xie discovered she had been defrauded, she reported it to the police, and RMB 3.35 million in illicit proceeds was recovered.

(2) Judgment

The Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, after trial, found that the defendant Huang Su'an, with intent to illegally appropriate property, used methods such as fabricating an identity and fabricating a high-return investment project to defraud the victim of RMB 7.05 million. His conduct constituted the crime of fraud, and the amount was particularly huge. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Criminal Law, the court found the defendant Huang Su'an guilty of fraud, sentencing him to life imprisonment and deprivation of political rights for life, and confiscation of all personal property. After the judgment was pronounced, the defendant Huang Su'an appealed. The Shanghai High People's Court, after trial in accordance with the law, ruled to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

(3) Typical Significance

This case is a typical example of fraud committed through dating websites. With the accelerating pace of urban work and life, professional dating websites have become a new platform for marriageable men and women, especially urban white-collar workers, to meet the opposite sex. However, due to low registration thresholds and difficulties in information verification, some dating websites have false information, making them susceptible to use by lawless persons for illegal activities. Some lawless persons register accounts on dating websites, use false identities to make friends, and after gaining the victim's trust, take the opportunity to commit theft, fraud, extortion, and even violent crimes such as rape and kidnapping. In this case, the defendant registered an account on a dating website, used the false identity of a "Chinese American" as a pretense and lure, and after winning the victim's favor and trust, defrauded her of a huge sum of money under the guise of investment and financial management. Although the defendant was ultimately severely punished by the law and part of the illicit proceeds were recovered, the emotional harm and huge property losses suffered by the victim are difficult to reverse. This case serves as a warning to the public to choose legitimate dating websites, carefully verify each other's identity and other information, and not easily part with money or emotional investment before confirming the other party's information.

3. Defendant Wang Daohong — Intentional Homicide

(1) Basic Facts

In early 2008, defendant Wang Daohong became acquainted through online chat with Liu (victim, died at age 33), a married woman, and they later developed a romantic relationship. In July 2009, Wang Daohong got a new girlfriend, who became pregnant. In November 2009, Wang Daohong met Liu as arranged and had sexual relations with her. The next day, Wang Daohong asked Liu to lend him RMB 5,000, citing his girlfriend's pregnancy, but Liu refused. Wang Daohong became angry, and strangled Liu with his hands and a towel, and sealed her mouth and nose with adhesive tape, causing Liu's death by mechanical asphyxia. After burying Liu's body, Wang Daohong used Liu's mobile phone to send text messages to her family demanding money, but was unsuccessful.

(2) Judgment

The Changde Intermediate People's Court of Hunan Province, after trial, found that the defendant Wang Daohong, over a trivial matter, caused the victim's death by strangulation, and his conduct constituted the crime of intentional homicide. Wang Daohong's killing method was cruel, the consequences were serious, and after the killing he attempted to extort money from the victim's relatives. His subjective malignancy was extremely high, the circumstances of the crime were vile, and the offense was extremely serious. He should be severely punished in accordance with the law. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Criminal Law, the court found the defendant Wang Daohong guilty of intentional homicide, sentencing him to death and deprivation of political rights for life. After the judgment was pronounced, Wang Daohong appealed. The Hunan High People's Court, after trial in open court, dismissed the appeal, affirmed the original judgment, and reported the case to the Supreme People's Court for approval in accordance with the law. The Supreme People's Court, after review in accordance with the law, ruled to approve the death sentence for the defendant Wang Daohong.

(3) Typical Significance

Rapidly developing and widely applied Internet technology plays a vital role in modern life. However, the Internet also has drawbacks such as virtuality. It is reported that some popular domestic social networking software applications have hundreds of millions of registered users and tens of millions of online users. In real life, many people are addicted to online dating and even place their emotions entirely on the "lovers" they meet online, deceived by the "charm" displayed by these online lovers, and overly trusting of others. However, when the virtual network collides with reality, the true face of the lover is ultimately exposed, and many people wake up as if from a dream, regretting their initial actions. In this case, victim Liu, a married woman, met defendant Wang Daohong through online chat and developed a romantic relationship with him. By the time of the incident, Liu had been involved with the defendant for over a year, but she still could not truly understand or recognize the defendant's true temperament and character, ultimately leading to the tragedy. It is hoped that this case will alert the public not to be deceived by online romances and to be cautious in making online friends.

4. Defendants Xiao Kechen — Kidnapping and Rape

(1) Basic Facts

Defendants Xiao Kechen and Xiao Shengkun (separately prosecuted) planned to commit a kidnapping using the Internet and rented a house in Lishui Town, Nanhai District, Foshan City, Guangdong Province, for the crime. On the evening of June 13, 2013, Xiao Kechen, under the pretext of going out to play, lured the victim Liang (female, then aged 15), whom he had met through the "Shake" feature on WeChat, and together with Xiao Shengkun, deceived Liang into the rented house. The two threatened Liang with utility knives and bound her with adhesive tape. Xiao Shengkun searched Liang's handbag and found RMB 350 in cash and a Xiaomi mobile phone. During this time, Xiao Kechen forcibly raped Liang. Thereafter, the two contacted Liang's mother by phone, demanding and receiving a ransom of RMB 20,000, and then fled the scene.

(2) Judgment

The Nanhai District People's Court of Foshan City, Guangdong Province, after trial, found that the defendant Xiao Kechen, acting in concert with others, kidnapped another person for the purpose of extorting property, and during the kidnapping, contrary to the victim's will, forcibly had sexual relations with the victim. His conduct constituted the crimes of kidnapping and rape, and he should be punished for multiple crimes in accordance with the law. Xiao Kechen had previously been sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment for fraud, and committed another crime less than half a year after his release, constituting a recidivist, and should be punished severely in accordance with the law. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Criminal Law, the court found the defendant Xiao Kechen guilty of kidnapping, sentencing him to fixed-term imprisonment of 11 years, deprivation of political rights for three years, and a fine of RMB 10,000; guilty of rape, sentencing him to fixed-term imprisonment of four years and six months; and decided to execute a combined sentence of fixed-term imprisonment of 14 years, deprivation of political rights for three years, and a fine of RMB 10,000. After the judgment was pronounced, the defendant Xiao Kechen appealed. The Foshan Intermediate People's Court, after trial in accordance with the law, ruled to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

(3) Typical Significance

This case is a typical example of kidnapping and rape crimes committed through online dating. With the development and increasing prevalence of Internet applications, online social platforms, especially online chat tools, have brought great convenience to interpersonal communication. At the same time, due to their public, anonymous, and convenient nature, online dating has become a new platform for lawless persons to commit crimes, leading to an increasing trend in related criminal cases. Some young women and teenagers lack protective awareness and ability, often making them easy targets for unlawful infringement. In this case, defendant Xiao Kechen, acting in concert with another, premeditated a kidnapping, rented a crime scene in advance, used WeChat's search function to target a minor female netizen as the victim, lured her out under the pretext of going out to play, and then kidnapped and raped her. The nature of the crime was vile, the circumstances and consequences were serious, and the social harm was great. The defendant was also a recidivist. The People's Court, in accordance with the law, imposed a severe punishment for his crimes, demonstrating on the one hand the firm stance of the People's Court in cracking down on crimes committed via the Internet, and on the other hand, through real cases, warning the public to remain vigilant in online dating, not to trust strangers easily, and especially for the vast number of teenagers and young women, to continuously improve their protective awareness and ability to protect themselves and their families from harm to person and property.

5. Defendant Ye Zhenqiang — Kidnapping

(1) Basic Facts

In May 2010, defendants Ye Zhenqiang and Lu Haobao rented and lived together in Room 602, Building 6, Diesel Engine Factory Family Quarters, Renmin Road, Zhaoling District, Luohe City, Henan Province. Due to financial difficulties, Ye Zhenqiang conceived the idea of kidnapping someone to extort money. On the evening of October 23 of that year, Ye Zhenqiang met the victim Zhao (female, died at age 18) through QQ chat. The two met as arranged, and Ye Zhenqiang brought Zhao back to the rented room. While Zhao was asleep, Ye Zhenqiang used transparent adhesive tape and a bedsheet to wrap and immobilize Zhao. The next morning, Ye Zhenqiang used Zhao's mobile phone to call Zhao's parents demanding a ransom, and had Zhao speak with her parents. Because Zhao disclosed the address of the kidnapping during the call, the two defendants, fearing exposure, formed the intent to kill her to silence her. Lu Haobao held down Zhao's legs, and Ye Zhenqiang covered Zhao's mouth and nose with a towel and strangled her neck, causing Zhao's death by mechanical asphyxia, after which the two fled.

(2) Judgment

The Luohe Intermediate People's Court of Henan Province, after trial, found that the defendant Ye Zhenqiang kidnapped another person for the purpose of extorting property, and then, fearing the crime would be exposed, killed the victim. His conduct constituted the crime of kidnapping. Ye Zhenqiang played a principal role in the joint crime, and should be punished according to all the crimes he participated in. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Criminal Law, the court found the defendant Ye Zhenqiang guilty of kidnapping, sentencing him to death and deprivation of political rights for life, and confiscation of all personal property. Lu Haobao was found guilty of kidnapping and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of 13 years. After the judgment was pronounced, Ye Zhenqiang appealed. The Henan High People's Court, after trial in open court, dismissed the appeal, affirmed the original judgment, and reported the case to the Supreme People's Court for approval in accordance with the law. The Supreme People's Court, after review in accordance with the law, ruled to approve the death sentence for the defendant Ye Zhenqiang.

(3) Typical Significance

With the development of smartphones and the widespread use of various social software applications, online social interaction is ubiquitous. Social software is merely a tool, with no inherent right or wrong, good or bad; the key is how it is used. If used by lawless persons, it can become a tool for crime. The Internet cannot verify users' basic identity information, let alone check users' character. Criminals take advantage of this, concealing their true identities, playing various roles, and selecting and "luring" potential targets on the Internet. After gaining the victim's trust, they arrange a meeting to further their criminal purposes. From the cases arising from the Internet in recent years, it can be seen that serious criminal offenses such as fraud, robbery, theft, extortion, forced prostitution, and even rape and murder occur from time to time, which urgently require the attention and vigilance of netizens. In this case, defendant Ye Zhenqiang, for the purpose of kidnapping, sought a criminal target through the Internet, gained the trust of victim Zhao, lured Zhao to the rented residence, kidnapped Zhao, and ultimately brutally killed her. It is hoped that this case will awaken the vigilance of netizens who are enthusiastic about online dating, urging them to be cautious in making online friends and not to give criminals an opportunity.

6. Defendant Zhang Shengui — Rape

(1) Basic Facts

In mid-June 2012, defendant Zhang Shengui, under the alias "Zhang Xuechuan," met the victim Fan (female, then aged 18) through QQ. After a period of online chatting, the two gradually became familiar. Zhang Shengui repeatedly asked Fan to be his girlfriend, but was refused; Fan later agreed to be his "sister." On July 5 of that year, Zhang Shengui met Fan as arranged, and they went to a park, strolled, and shopped together. After lunch, Zhang Shengui, on the pretext that the weather was too hot, suggested going to a hotel to shower and asked Fan to come along, repeatedly requesting that Fan wait until he finished showering before leaving, to which Fan agreed. They then went to a hotel, and Zhang Shengui, claiming he did not have his ID card, used Fan's ID card to check in. After showering, Zhang Shengui locked the door, took a knife from his pocket, threatened Fan into becoming his girlfriend, and forced Fan to undress. Seeing this, Fan tried to call for help. Zhang Shengui snatched her phone, raped her, and took several nude photos of Fan with his phone.

(2) Judgment

The Jianyang People's Court of Fujian Province, after trial, found that the defendant Zhang Shengui, contrary to the will of a woman, used coercive means to forcibly have sexual relations with the victim, and his conduct constituted the crime of rape. Zhang Shengui had previously been sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment for rape, and within five years after serving that sentence, he committed another crime punishable by fixed-term imprisonment or more, constituting a recidivist, and should be punished severely in accordance with the law. Given that Zhang Shengui had fully compensated the victim for all economic losses, a lighter punishment could be imposed at discretion. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Criminal Law, the court found the defendant Zhang Shengui guilty of rape, sentencing him to fixed-term imprisonment of four years and six months. After the judgment was pronounced, the defendant Zhang Shengui appealed. The Nanping Intermediate People's Court of Fujian Province, after trial in accordance with the law, ruled to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

(3) Typical Significance

Today, QQ chatting has become part of the lives of most young people; it shortens the time and space distance between people and enriches their leisure and cultural life. However, while bringing convenience to people's work and life, it also creates opportunities for lawless persons to commit crimes. Some people specifically use QQ online to seek targets for illegal acts, including online fraud and violent crimes. Young people with little life experience are particularly susceptible to deception and being misled by lies fabricated through the virtual communication method of QQ. To purify cyberspace and protect the legitimate rights and interests of citizens, especially minors, crimes committed through the Internet must be severely cracked down upon. In this case, defendant Zhang Shengui met Fan, who had just graduated from high school, through QQ, gained her trust, arranged a meeting, and then under the pretext of taking a shower, deceived Fan into getting a hotel room together, where he raped her. The occurrence of this case reminds the public not to trust people met through the Internet, not to disclose personal information online, and especially not to meet netizens alone to avoid danger.

7. Defendants Zhao Xiaoming et al. — Unlawful Detention

(1) Basic Facts

From March 2011, defendants Zhao Xiaoming, Cao Jinsheng, Zhang Leliang, and others gathered in Room 501, West Unit 1, No. 29 Yongxingdao Road, Huangdao District, Qingdao City, Shandong Province, to engage in pyramid scheme activities, with Zhao Xiaoming serving as the business director in charge of daily management. On August 22 of that year, Zhang Leliang, under the pretext of helping find a job, lured the victim Jiang (female, then aged 20) through QQ chat to the room where they conducted pyramid scheme activities. Zhao Xiaoming then arranged for Cao Jinsheng, Zhang Leliang, and others to give Jiang lectures on pyramid schemes and to keep close watch to prevent Jiang from leaving. In the early morning of August 25, Jiang, realizing she had been tricked into joining a pyramid scheme, attempted to escape by climbing out of a window of the room, but fell to her death.

(2) Judgment

The Huangdao District People's Court of Qingdao City, Shandong Province, after trial, found that the defendants Zhao Xiaoming, Cao Jinsheng, and Zhang Leliang unlawfully restricted another person's personal freedom, and their conduct constituted the crime of unlawful detention. Zhao Xiaoming committed a crime during the probation period for a suspended sentence, so the suspended sentence should be revoked and multiple punishments combined; he played a principal role in the joint crime and was the principal offender. Zhang Leliang and Cao Jinsheng were accomplices. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Criminal Law, the court found the defendant Zhao Xiaoming guilty of unlawful detention, and combined the punishment with that for the previous crime, deciding to execute a sentence of fixed-term imprisonment of 11 years and deprivation of political rights for one year; the defendant Zhang Leliang was found guilty of unlawful detention and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of nine years; the defendant Cao Jinsheng was found guilty of unlawful detention and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of seven years. The judgment has now taken legal effect.

(3) Typical Significance

This case is a typical example where a young woman was forced to participate in pyramid scheme activities through unlawful detention, resulting in her death. With the rapid development of network technology, cases where pyramid scheme organizations are established and crimes are committed using the Internet are increasing. In this case, the victim Jiang was seeking a job online, unfortunately caught the attention of pyramid scheme members, was unlawfully detained, and eventually died while attempting to escape, which is deeply regrettable.
